en.title: Longest Subsequence Increasing by One Each Step
en.description:
Choose an order-preserving subsequence of the integer array in which each subsequent element is exactly 1 greater than the previous one. Output the maximum length. The elements do not need to be contiguous.

The standard input/output, examples, and tests are written by CSWork; ranges marked "this site" are judging conventions and are not claimed to be original interview limits.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..100000); the second line contains n integers (−10⁹..10⁹).
en.output: Output the answer as described; results for multiple queries are separated by spaces, in order.
en.explanation: Example 1: you can pick 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in order, for a length of 5. Example 2: the array is strictly decreasing, so no element one larger can follow in order; the answer is 1. Example 3: repeated numbers cannot be chosen one after another; choosing 1, 2, 3 gives 3.
hints: dp[v] is the best length of a subsequence ending with v in the current prefix. When the scan reaches v, update dp[v] with dp[v−1]+1.
